A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMR research and have 12 readable pages. All text, equations, figures, tables, and references support comparison; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. Pages 2–12 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMR experiments on QVHighlights, Charades-STA, and TACoS, including benchmark results, component ablations, and qualitative comparisons in Tables 1–4 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, component ablations, and qualitative comparisons in Tables 1–4 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical Splice-and-Boost augmentation, cold-start training, dual-path distillation, query architecture, and loss functions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate moment retrieval on QVHighlights, Charades-STA, and TACoS. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3, including BAM-DETR in Table 1 and UVCOM in Table 2. Figure 4 retains comparisons with UVCOM and TaskWeave.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same evaluation splits, metrics, feature encoders, and training settings, including 40 first-stage epochs and 100 second-stage epochs.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains all 12 component-ablation configurations. The backbone comparisons in Table 3 and three qualitative cases in Figure 4 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 reports AMR average mAP of 51.66 on QVHighlights validation and 48.43 on test in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, hard-negative selection conditions, and Equations (1)–(7) are identical. Neither version introduces additional propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about zero-external-dependency augmentation, two-stage knowledge transfer, and improved moment-retrieval performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of augmented-to-real distribution mismatch, forgetting, component effectiveness, and semantic and boundary discrimination are unchanged. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code repository address from github.com/nagara214/AMR to github.com/SooLab/AMR. Implementation details and hardware disclosures remain identical; the PDFs do not establish any change in repository contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and references [1]–[82] are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to architecture improvements, pretraining, and external data synthesis.

P1.justification: The first-page repository text and arXiv version/date stamp are updated. Scientific wording, terminology, headings, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract has different line wrapping, and the first-page arXiv stamp changes. Figures 1–4, Tables 1–4, their captions, and the layout of pages 2–12 remain identical.

improvement.justification: The revision changes the repository address and minor first-page presentation while retaining identical methods, evidence, explanations, and conclusions. The PDFs do not establish that the new address resolves a code-access problem, so the documented changes provide no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
